Interface InstanceWatchRequest<T>

Type Parameters:
T - The bean type
public interface InstanceWatchRequest<T>
A request to watch the beans of the definitions a DefinitionWatchRequest selected, continued with DefinitionWatchRequest.instances(), and completed by watch(BeanInstanceWatcher) or watch(). The watch creates the beans: it receives them as its first batch, then one batch per change, with the instances that went and the ones that came. The instances delivered stay the ones delivered: a prototype among the candidates is created once for the watch, not again for every batch. 
context.definitions(Rule.class).instances()
    .onAdded(registration -> rules.add(registration.bean()))
    .onRemoved(registration -> rules.remove(registration.bean()))
    .watch();

Who destroys an instance delivered:

  • A bean no scope holds, such as a prototype, is created for the watch, which owns it: the watch destroys it, its @PreDestroy methods and the dependent beans it owns included, once the batch that removes it was delivered, or when the watch is closed, by BeanWatch.close(), with the bean that registered the watch, or when the context stops. The watcher does not destroy it, and does not use a removed instance after the batch that removed it, nor any instance after the watch was closed.
  • A singleton, or a bean of a custom scope, belongs to its scope, which destroys it as it would without the watch: a removed one may already be destroyed, or still be in use elsewhere.

Each terminal operation takes a snapshot of the request, so a request may be reused for further watches.

    • onRemoved

      InstanceWatchRequest<T> onRemoved(Consumer<? super BeanRegistration<T>> handler)
      Adds a handler called with each bean removed, once the batch that removes it is applied, and before the watch destroys an instance it owns. A bean replaced by one of a new generation of its definition is given to onReplaced(Consumer) instead, when there is such a handler.
      Parameters:
      handler - The handler
      Returns:
      This request

    • onReplaced

      InstanceWatchRequest<T> onReplaced(Consumer<? super BeanInstanceChange.Replacement<T>> handler)
      Adds a handler called with each bean removed and replaced by the bean of a new generation of its definition. Without this handler, the bean is given to onRemoved(Consumer) and its replacement to onAdded(Consumer).
      Parameters:
      handler - The handler
      Returns:
      This request
